FUNERAL PRICE LIST CHECKER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Which funeral charges are required, and which are your choice?

Paste the lines from a funeral home's General Price List or quote. Each priced line is sorted into the fee you cannot decline, what is usually needed, what is your choice and what is paid to someone else, with charges the FTC Funeral Rule speaks to flagged. Paste a second home to compare line by line.

Nothing is uploaded. The page makes no network calls. It is a reading aid and not legal advice.

Home A: paste a price list or quote

Compare with a second home (optional)

Paste a list and click Check the list.

Result

LineTypePrice

Questions to ask the funeral home

    Home A against Home B

    Kind of chargeTypeHome AHome B

    A kind of charge only one home lists is the usual reason two totals differ: check whether the other home folds it into another line or does not offer it.

    Run it from the command line

    node cli.mjs quote.txt
node cli.mjs --compare home-a.txt home-b.txt
node cli.mjs --example

    Get cli.mjs and funeral.mjs from the repo. Node 18+, no dependencies.

    Common questions

    What is the FTC Funeral Rule?

    A US federal rule (16 CFR 453) that requires funeral homes to give you an itemized General Price List to keep, quote prices by phone, let you buy only the items you want, accept a casket or urn you bought elsewhere without a fee, and not tell you a service is required by law when it is not. It does not cap prices.

    Is embalming required by law?

    Not by federal law. A few states require it in narrow cases, such as certain kinds of transport or a long delay before burial or viewing. A funeral home may not say it is required unless a law says so, and needs your permission before charging for it. Ask which law applies and whether refrigeration would do.

    Do I have to buy a casket for cremation?

    No. No casket is required for cremation. A home that offers direct cremation must offer an alternative container, such as unfinished wood or heavy cardboard.

    Can a funeral home charge a fee because I bought the casket elsewhere?

    Under the FTC Funeral Rule, no. A home must accept a casket or urn you bought elsewhere and may not charge a handling or inspection fee for it. The checker flags any line that looks like one.

    Which fee can I not decline?

    The basic services fee. It is the one charge the Rule lets a funeral home require, and what it covers differs by home, so compare it across homes.

    Does the checker tell me what a fair price is?

    No. It sorts each priced line into what it is, adds up each group and compares two homes line by line, so you can see which items are your choice. Prices differ by region and home, and the tool is not legal advice.

    Is my price list uploaded anywhere?

    No. Everything runs in this page and the page makes no network calls.

    More: What the FTC Funeral Rule gives you, and what it does not

    No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It sorts text by keywords and can misread a line; the funeral home's own price list is authoritative. This is not legal, financial or funeral-planning advice, and state rules differ. You are responsible for confirming each charge with the funeral home, and with your state regulator if a charge looks wrong, before you rely on it.

    Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record. If a tool needs to survive, get cli.mjs from the repo and run it yourself.

    Everything runs in your browser. The prices you paste are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors, and the tool makes no network calls. Anonymous feature events (list_checked, homes_compared, questions_copied, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage and can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

    Related tools: Estate Sale Net Proceeds Calculator and Estate Tax Exemption Calculator.

    Free and open source. If this saved a family some money, the code is under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional and never changes what the tool does.

← Funeral Price List Checker

What the FTC Funeral Rule gives you, and what it does not

When someone has just died, families often decide quickly, in an unfamiliar office, with a person selling to them. The Funeral Rule (16 CFR 453, enforced by the US Federal Trade Commission) exists for that moment. It is about information and choice. It does not set prices.

What you are entitled to

  • An itemized General Price List you can keep, handed to you when you start talking about arrangements, in person.
  • Prices by phone. A home must give prices over the phone to a caller who asks, without requiring your name or address first.
  • Only what you choose. You may buy individual items rather than a package, with one exception below.
  • An outside casket or urn. A home must accept a casket or urn you bought elsewhere, and may not charge a handling fee for it.
  • An alternative container for cremation. A home that offers direct cremation must offer a plain container, so no casket is needed.
  • No false claims of legal requirement. A home must not say embalming, a particular casket or a vault is required by law when it is not, and must tell you what is actually required.
  • Permission before embalming in most cases, and a clear explanation of what it is.

What it does not give you

  • A cap on prices. The same service can cost very different amounts at two homes a few miles apart, which is why comparing is worth an afternoon.
  • The right to decline the basic services fee. It is the one fee a home may require. It is also where homes differ most in what they put inside it.
  • Rules for cemeteries or crematories. A cemetery can require an outer burial container or sell its own plot rules, and the Rule does not cover cemeteries that are not also funeral providers.

Five questions that save money

  1. What exactly is in the basic services fee, and what is the total for exactly the choices I have made?
  2. Which of these lines does a law require, and which law?
  3. What would this cost with a plain container, or a casket I bought elsewhere?
  4. Which of the cash-advance items do you add a charge to?
  5. Can I have this quote in writing, and the same quote from your other price tiers?

Use the checker

Paste the lines of a price list or quote into the checker. It sorts each priced line into what you cannot decline, what is usually needed and what is your choice, flags the charges above, and lists the questions to put to the home. Paste a second home to compare them line by line.

No warranty. Provided free and as-is. A plain-language summary of a federal rule, not professional or legal advice; the regulation and your state's laws govern. If you think a funeral home broke the Rule, you can report it to the FTC and to your state's funeral regulator. Best-effort hosting, no SLA. The page makes no network calls and uploads nothing. Check a price list.
